content: 1. The study by Marques et al. (2022) evaluates the use of methylxanthine for the prevention and treatment of apnea in preterm infants. The certainty of evidence was assessed, considering factors such as risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias. The findings indicate a reduction of 89 cases per 1000 (ranging from 149 fewer to 12 fewer cases per 1000) with an overall certainty of evidence rated as moderate. 2. North et al. (2022) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on family involvement in the routine care of hospitalized preterm or low birth weight infants. The study assessed the impact of family involvement compared to usual hospital care. The results showed a reduction of 7 cases per 1000 (ranging from 19 fewer to 15 more cases per 1000), with the overall certainty of evidence rated as low. 3. Bedwell et al. (2022) reviewed interventions to support parents, families, and caregivers in caring for premature or low birth weight infants at home. The study compared education and counseling interventions to usual care. The findings indicated an increase in infant length at 60 days follow-up, with a certainty of evidence rated as moderate. 4. The same study by Bedwell et al. (2022) also evaluated peer support interventions versus usual care. The results demonstrated an improvement in mother-infant interaction at 6 weeks of age, assessed using the NCAST Feeding Scale, with a certainty of evidence rated as moderate. 5. Another comparison in Bedwell et al. (2022) focused on discharge preparation versus usual care. The findings showed an increase in the duration of exclusive breastfeeding (measured in weeks), with the certainty of evidence rated as moderate. 6. Bedwell et al. (2022) also assessed the impact of digital information systems compared to usual care. The results indicated a positive effect on parental confidence and caregiving ability, with the certainty of evidence rated as moderate. 7. Lastly, Bedwell et al. (2022) examined the effect of home visits to support families in providing care for premature or low birth weight infants compared to usual care. The findings showed an improvement in infant health outcomes, with the certainty of evidence rated as moderate.
